subject.title: [Feature]: Multi-role support in Chat UI for multi-agent workflows

question: Should OpenClaw add a durable per-message sender identity contract for multi-agent chat, and what sender metadata shape should become the gateway/session/UI API?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the fix defines a cross-surface product/API contract rather than a narrow bug repair; automation should not invent the persisted sender schema or compatibility behavior.

options.title: Add durable sender metadata
options.body: Adopt an additive sender identity object across protocol, transcript, history/live events, subagent announce delivery, and Control UI rendering while preserving existing `senderLabel` projections as compatibility/display hints.

options.title: Keep label-only partials
options.body: Continue landing narrow fixes such as requester-name prompt context and blank-label fallbacks without committing to a durable identity contract yet.

options.title: Split into smaller contracts
options.body: Create separate canonical issues for protocol/transcript identity, subagent announce identity, and Control UI avatar rendering before implementation.

recommendation.title: Add durable sender metadata
recommendation.body: Adopt an additive sender identity object across protocol, transcript, history/live events, subagent announce delivery, and Control UI rendering while preserving existing `senderLabel` projections as compatibility/display hints.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history across inter-session provenance, session-send context, and the current protocol/session surfaces that would define the contract.
